accepted_examples.german: Wie kannst du nur so gelassen sein?
accepted_examples.english: How can you be so calm?
accepted_examples.note: gelassen means calm here, and the question and translation match directly.

accepted_examples.german: Der Plan ist ohne Sinn und Verstand.
accepted_examples.english: There's no rhyme or reason to that plan.
accepted_examples.note: Verstand is used in the idiom ohne Sinn und Verstand; the translation no rhyme or reason captures the same idea.

accepted_examples.german: Mein Rat an Sie ist, sofort zu gehen.
accepted_examples.english: My advice to you is to leave immediately.
accepted_examples.note: Rat means advice/counsel, and the English translation states the same recommendation.

accepted_examples.german: Es hat keinen Sinn, eine Kamera mitzubringen.
accepted_examples.english: There's no point in taking a camera.
accepted_examples.note: Kamera is the device for taking photographs or filming; the translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Ich habe meine Schuhe ausgelatscht.
accepted_examples.english: I've worn out my shoes.
accepted_examples.note: Schuhe is the regular plural form of Schuh, and the sentence and translation describe wearing shoes out.

accepted_examples.german: Herzlichen Glückwunsch! Sie haben gewonnen.
accepted_examples.english: Congratulations! You won.
accepted_examples.note: Glückwunsch is used in the conventional congratulatory phrase; the translation is idiomatic.

accepted_examples.german: Ich entschied mich, zu gehen, statt zu bleiben.
accepted_examples.english: I chose to leave instead of staying behind.
accepted_examples.note: statt zu bleiben expresses instead of staying, matching the English sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Keiner seiner beiden Söhne wollte das Geschäft übernehmen.
accepted_examples.english: Neither of his sons wanted to take over the business.
accepted_examples.note: übernehmen means take over in the business context, matching the English translation.

accepted_examples.german: Der See ist der tiefste in dieser Gegend.
accepted_examples.english: The lake is deepest in this area.
accepted_examples.note: Gegend means area/region and is used naturally with dieser.

accepted_examples.german: Gehen Sie nicht zu weit in den Wald!
accepted_examples.english: Don't go too far into the woods.
accepted_examples.note: Wald means forest/woods; the imperative and translation align.

accepted_examples.german: Ich hätte sehr gerne ein kaltes Glas Bier.
accepted_examples.english: I would love a cold glass of beer.
accepted_examples.note: Glas means a drinking glass here and the English translation matches.

accepted_examples.german: Bist du denn nicht dafür verantwortlich?
accepted_examples.english: Aren't you in charge?
accepted_examples.note: verantwortlich means in charge/responsible here; dafür is reflected in the translation.

accepted_examples.german: Tom begann vor Schmerz zu stöhnen.
accepted_examples.english: Tom started moaning in pain.
accepted_examples.note: stöhnen means moan/groan, and the pain context is accurately translated.

accepted_examples.german: Dieser Hut passt zum Kleid.
accepted_examples.english: This hat goes together with the dress.
accepted_examples.note: Kleid means dress; passen zu expresses that one item goes with another, as translated.

accepted_examples.german: Abendessen wird zwischen neun Uhr und Mitternacht serviert.
accepted_examples.english: The evening meal is served between 9 and 12.
accepted_examples.note: Abendessen means the evening meal; the sentence and English translation agree.

accepted_examples.german: Die Mehrheit des Ausschusses stimmte gegen das Gesetz.
accepted_examples.english: The majority of the committee voted against the bill.
accepted_examples.note: Gesetz is used for legislation under discussion; bill is a context-appropriate English rendering in the committee vote.

accepted_examples.german: Wir gehen schon drei Jahre gemeinsam aus.
accepted_examples.english: We've been going out with each other for three years.
accepted_examples.note: gemeinsam means together; the sentence expresses a shared activity and the English translation preserves that sense.

accepted_examples.german: Eine tausend Meilen lange Reise beginnt mit einem einzigen Schritt.
accepted_examples.english: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
accepted_examples.note: Schritt means a step in a process; the proverb uses it literally as the first step on a journey.

accepted_examples.german: Bitte bring das Band morgen zurück.
accepted_examples.english: Please bring back the tape tomorrow.
accepted_examples.note: Band means tape in this context, and the translation explicitly selects that sense.

accepted_examples.german: Es hat ungefähr die Größe von einem Ei.
accepted_examples.english: It's about the size of an egg.
accepted_examples.note: ungefähr means approximately/about, with the size comparison accurately translated.

held_examples.german: Ein Soldat muß sich oft der Gefahr stellen.
held_examples.reason: The candidate uses the superseded spelling muß; use current standard spelling for learner-facing material.

held_examples.german: Den 30 Passagieren an Bord geht es allen gut.
held_examples.reason: An Bord means aboard/on board, which is unrelated to the selected shelf sense of Bord.

held_examples.german: Sie nahmen einen Mann namens Lee Harvey Oswald fest.
held_examples.reason: Lee is only a surname in this sentence and does not demonstrate the nautical lee-side meaning.

held_examples.german: Jeder scheint dem Achtung zu schenken, was er sagt.
held_examples.reason: The candidate word order is faulty for the intended structure and does not provide a reliable model sentence.

held_examples.german: He, guckt mal, was ich kann!
held_examples.reason: The opening interjection He is a typo or malformed punctuation; replace it with a clean colloquial imperative.

editorial_examples.german: Ein Soldat muss im Einsatz oft schwierige Entscheidungen treffen.
editorial_examples.english: A soldier often has to make difficult decisions in the field.
editorial_examples.note: Current German spelling and a complete neutral sentence.

editorial_examples.german: Das Bord aus Holz über dem Schreibtisch ist sehr praktisch.
editorial_examples.english: The wooden shelf above the desk is very practical.
editorial_examples.note: This demonstrates Bord in the selected shelf sense, not the phrase an Bord.

editorial_examples.german: Das Schiff suchte im Lee der Insel Schutz vor dem Wind.
editorial_examples.english: The ship sought shelter from the wind on the lee side of the island.
editorial_examples.note: The noun Lee is used in its nautical sense, with a clear contextual cue.

editorial_examples.german: Bitte schenken Sie den Sicherheitsanweisungen besondere Achtung.
editorial_examples.english: Please pay special attention to the safety instructions.
editorial_examples.note: Correct, natural noun use of Achtung in the attention sense.
A short, grammatical informal imperative that clearly demonstrates gucken.
